newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures slip again late, most end weaker.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures slip again late, most end weaker.

text.p: U.S. debt futures slipped again late and most ended spotty pit trading weaker after the market gave up on a quick recovery sparked by economic commentary from the Federal Reserve.
June Treasury bond futures eroded back to moderate losses and ended near day's lows after small-size sales from a few dealers scared locals into bailing out of longs, brokers said.
"There was not a lot there," said one floor broker. "People got caught long."
Nearby T-bonds closed near Tuesday's low after the final drop but managed to stave off a break below 109-16/32 support.

"We're still settling in neutral territory but under pressure technically," the floor broker added. "The 109-16/32 (level) is an obvious area because that is where the market established a base after Friday's spike up. We would need to settle under 16 (109-16/32) to really come under pressure."

Brokers said the Fed's Beige Book, prepared this time by the St Louis bank and based on interviews with businessmen conducted before March 3, was supportive but revealed little that the market found unexpected or exciting.
The report said U.S. price pressures are temperate, partly because of stiff competition.

It said wage gains were moderate and showed no signs of breaking out of the three-percent to four-percent range of the last several reports. It also said nearly every district reported difficulty finding and keeping new employees.
"It doesn't seem to deviate from other recent Beige Books," said John Nyhoff, chief economist, Tokyo-Mitsubishi Futures (USA) Inc.

He said the Beige Book likely did little to change players' opinions about nearterm direction, with short-term debt futures not pricing in any tightening until May rather than at the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"So I think the market's still leaning toward tightening in May," Nyhoff said, "So there's no immediate sense of urgency that the Fed has to do something right away."

Retail sales Thursday are seen rising 0.6 percent, with the ex-autos component expected to rise 0.7 percent. Weekly jobless claims are seen rising 3,000 to 313,000 from the prior week's original 310,000 level. February's Atlanta Fed index was postponed until Thursday at 0900 CST/1500 GMT.

June T-bonds lost 11/32 to 109-21/32, T-notes lost 5/32 to 107-12/32, munis fell 9/32 to 113-14/32, Sept T-bills lost 0.02 bps to 94.535, and Sept Eurodollars lost 0.025 to 93.980. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
